title: APPSC Group 2 Mains Paper II · Model 1
provenance: GateLabs original mock based on Notification 37/2026, Annexure II. Separate paper with 75 questions in each of its two sections. Includes recall and applied questions. Chapter counts are editorial practice choices.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: What does a current-account deficit mean by itself?
options: A country has no financial inflows
Every imported product costs more than its exported counterpart
Government spending exceeds all tax revenue
Current-account payments exceed receipts under the balance of payments convention
questions.explanation: The current account includes goods, services and specified income flows and transfers.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which factor directly lowers firms' transaction costs in regulatory compliance?
questions.explanation: Predictability and fewer duplications can lower compliance costs.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Why do irrigated deltas and semi-arid uplands often have different crop mixes?
options: Water availability and local production conditions differ
All input costs are legally fixed at one level
Only national population explains crop choice
questions.explanation: Water, soils, market access and risk affect crop decisions.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: Which comparison best separates nominal rates from actual realised budget figures?
options: Assume no exemptions affect the base
Treat every budget estimate as audited
Read the enacted rate and compare revenue receipts in the relevant statement
Infer tax collections from the announced rate alone
questions.explanation: Realised receipts depend on the tax base and compliance as well as statutory rates.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which infrastructure primarily improves connectivity over a production corridor?
options: An increase in book sales without logistics changes
Integrated freight, power and logistics networks
questions.explanation: Corridors connect clusters and markets through supporting infrastructure.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: Which is an example of a capital expenditure when classified accordingly?
options: Construction creating a new public asset
questions.explanation: Expenditure creating a public asset is commonly recorded as capital outlay.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: A state diverts funds from maintenance to new asset creation. Which indicator most directly records the classification change?
options: Time series of all participating banks
questions.explanation: The relevant budget breakdown shows movement between revenue and capital heads.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Output rises while school completion and health outcomes stagnate. What distinction matters?
questions.explanation: Development includes outcomes beyond aggregate output.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What does ITES mean in services-sector discussions?
questions.explanation: ITES refers to services supported or delivered through information technology.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Which description best fits NITI Aayog?
options: Policy institution and platform for cooperative federalism
Central bank responsible for issuing banknotes
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog supports policy analysis and cooperative federalism.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: What distinguishes current-price GDP from constant-price GDP?
options: Current-price GDP uses prices prevailing in the measured period
Constant-price GDP uses only interest rates
questions.explanation: Nominal output uses prevailing prices; constant prices permit volume comparisons.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which risk is most direct for a rainfed crop exposed to erratic monsoon onset?
options: Foreign exchange reserves automatically fall by the same proportion
Planting may be delayed or establishment can fail
All monsoon variability raises yield simultaneously
questions.explanation: Rainfed crops depend on moisture at critical growth stages.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Using the expenditure approach, how are imports treated in GDP?
options: They are excluded from all purchased goods before any accounting
They count as domestic value added in full
They are subtracted as part of net exports
questions.explanation: Subtracting imports removes foreign production included in domestic expenditure.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What can make a port-adjacent manufacturing location attractive?
options: Lower handling costs for imported inputs or outbound shipments
A guaranteed solution to every labour shortage
No need for electricity or water
Identical freight costs for every location
questions.explanation: Proximity to port and freight connections can reduce some logistics costs.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: What does destination-based taxation of consumption generally emphasise?
options: The country issuing a company's shares
The location of any intermediate raw material in all cases
The jurisdiction of consumption or supply destination
questions.explanation: Destination-based taxes attach revenue to consumption destinations under applicable rules.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What can a cooperative credit institution help pool?
options: Local savings and lending relationships for members
questions.explanation: Member-based institutions can pool resources and provide local credit.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: Which comparison best measures the difference between a year's original allocation and final recorded spending?
options: Two revised estimates from future years
questions.explanation: Budget estimates are plans. Actuals show recorded spending for the year.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: What does a revised estimate indicate in a budget document?
options: An updated estimate for a year whose outcome may still be incomplete
A proposal solely for a future year
An accounting period that omits spending
questions.explanation: A revised estimate updates the original budget estimate for a period.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: If real GDP grows 6% and population grows 2%, approximate real per-capita growth is what?
questions.explanation: Divide the output growth factor 1.06 by population growth factor 1.02 and subtract one.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: How should an announced AP IT policy's period be verified?
options: Date it from the first social media post alone
Read the issued policy and applicable government orders
Use a different state's industrial notification
questions.explanation: The actual instrument establishes scope and duration.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Output rises with area unchanged. Which measure must have risen?
questions.explanation: With a fixed area the change in output comes from higher output per unit of area.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: For a consistent growth comparison, what should be checked first about two published GSDP figures?
options: Use a comparable price basis, reference period and series
Use the one with the higher numerical value
questions.explanation: Comparability depends on prices, methodology and period.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: A sector has 40% of employment and 20% of aggregate output. What follows under comparable measures?
options: Each worker earns exactly half the national average wage
Its average output per worker is half the economy-wide average
The sector has 40% of total productivity
The national price level is unchanged
questions.explanation: The ratio of output share to employment share gives relative average output per worker.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which metric can assess loss during transport in a fisheries value chain?
options: Spoilage or quality loss as a share of the quantity shipped
Number of service categories in the constitution
questions.explanation: Physical and quality losses directly measure cold-chain or handling performance.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: A budget records expenditure 700, tax and other non-debt receipts 560, and interest 50. What is fiscal deficit?
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit here is 700 − 560 = 140.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What does issue price refer to in a food distribution context?
options: The exchange rate for agricultural imports
Price at which stocks are supplied under the specified arrangement
questions.explanation: Issue prices concern release or distribution of procured stocks.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: Which adjustment forms an average per-capita measure?
options: Divide the specified income or output aggregate by population
Divide all state revenue by exports only
questions.explanation: Per-capita amounts are divided by the relevant population.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Why does crop area alone fail to measure production?
options: Prices determine physical output by definition
Yield per unit of area also matters
Every crop has the same yield
Area automatically includes the full quantity harvested
questions.explanation: Production equals area times yield.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: If total interest paid rises, which expenditure component is directly affected?
options: Interest payments within the appropriate revenue expenditure head
Own tax receipts by the same amount
questions.explanation: Interest constitutes an expenditure commitment in public finance.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Which quantity best measures an occupational share?
options: Sector value added divided by all expenditure
Total crop area divided by population
Workers in an activity divided by total workers under the same definition
questions.explanation: Occupational shares use employment counts, not output.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: What makes public debt different from fiscal deficit?
options: Debt is a flow and deficit a stock
Debt is a stock and deficit is a flow
Debt equals annual interest payments only
questions.explanation: Debt is measured at a date while fiscal deficit accumulates over a period.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What does agricultural credit primarily enable?
options: Eliminating physical crop risk by itself
Paying for inputs and investment over time
questions.explanation: Credit helps bridge the timing gap between expenses and receipts.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: Which is a likely first-channel effect of tighter monetary policy, other factors equal?
options: Immediate direct increase in government expenditure
Lower legal reserve requirements in every case
questions.explanation: Tighter policy generally works through financing conditions and demand.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What is disinvestment in a public-enterprise context?
options: Purchase of additional inventory by a factory
Issuing currency to replace old notes
Sale of part or all of a government's equity stake
An increase in depreciation allowances alone
questions.explanation: Disinvestment concerns government shareholdings.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: How does FDI differ conceptually from passive portfolio holdings?
options: It can occur only in agriculture
It is the same as an import of goods
It is necessarily a grant from a foreign government
It is associated with lasting interest or significant influence under statistical definitions
questions.explanation: Direct investment is distinguished by the investor's lasting interest in the enterprise.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Why might regional industry clusters arise near one another?
options: Shared suppliers, labour pools and infrastructure
A requirement that all sectors use identical inputs
questions.explanation: Agglomeration can lower costs and improve access to expertise and services.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: Inter-state supplies under the Indian GST framework generally involve which component?
options: Only SGST levied independently by both states on the same transaction
A stamp duty on all supplies
questions.explanation: Integrated GST applies to inter-state taxable supplies under the framework.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Why check whether GDP is a provisional or revised estimate?
options: Provisional values cannot be expressed in rupees
Later releases may incorporate more complete source data
Actual GDP is reported only by courts
Revision means all growth measures become forecasts
questions.explanation: National accounts can be updated when fuller or revised source data are available.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which pairing typically matches Indian crop seasons?
options: Kharif with the summer monsoon and rabi with the cooler season
Rabi with the summer monsoon and kharif with winter sowing
Kharif only with annual factory shutdowns
Both with identical sowing calendars everywhere
questions.explanation: Kharif cultivation generally follows the summer monsoon, while rabi crops grow in the cool season.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: How is primary deficit ordinarily obtained?
questions.explanation: Primary deficit removes interest payments from fiscal deficit.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Which adjustment converts a gross aggregate to a net aggregate?
questions.explanation: Net national-account aggregates deduct consumption of fixed capital.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: Which function of money lets it express prices in a common denomination?
questions.explanation: The unit of account provides a shared scale for prices and obligations.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: What is revenue deficit?
questions.explanation: Revenue deficit compares expenditure and receipts on the revenue account.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: Which is normally an example of state non-tax revenue?
options: Fees and user charges recorded under non-tax heads
Proceeds of shareable central income tax
questions.explanation: Government service fees and user charges commonly fall under non-tax receipts.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which symptom can indicate industrial sickness without identifying its cause?
options: Persistent inability to meet financial obligations
Opening a new export warehouse with rising sales
questions.explanation: Financial distress is a symptom; causes require separate investigation.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which linkage can help MSMEs scale production?
options: Reliable supplier relationships and access to finance
Replacing invoices with informal promises in every case
questions.explanation: Finance and supply-chain links help firms respond to demand and procure inputs.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which is a key allied-sector activity for the AP coast?
options: Coal mining everywhere along the coast
questions.explanation: Coastal and brackish areas provide suitable locations for parts of the fisheries sector.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: Why inspect both the Annual Financial Statement and demanded grants?
options: One gives only inflation and the other only export totals
They must always have different financial years
One shows aggregate fiscal plans and the other details allocations to demands
questions.explanation: Together the statements expose aggregate and spending-level detail.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Which sector normally includes banking and retail?
questions.explanation: Financial and retail activities are services.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Which reform was a prominent component of India's 1991 industrial changes?
options: Mandatory licensing for every new firm
Replacement of all banks by a single bank
Removal of licensing requirements in many industries
questions.explanation: The reforms reduced the reach of industrial licensing.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Which term distinguishes GNI from GDP?
options: Net primary income from the rest of the world
questions.explanation: GNI adds net primary income across borders to GDP.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which facility most directly slows post-harvest deterioration in perishable produce?
questions.explanation: Temperature-controlled storage extends the usable distribution time of many perishable foods.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What is the main purpose of an industrial single-window system?
options: Coordinate approval applications through a common channel
Set the price of every product
Automatically exempt all projects from statutory requirements
questions.explanation: Single-window systems facilitate handling of approvals without eliminating statutory obligations.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: Which scenario most directly represents cost-push inflation?
options: A change in the calendar of statistical releases
A fall in production costs and selling prices
A one-time fall in prices due to ample supply
A broad input-cost shock raises selling prices
questions.explanation: Rising costs can put upward pressure on prices even without stronger demand.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Why can access to storage improve a grower’s marketing choice?
options: It fixes all spot market prices nationally
It always replaces the need for credit
It can reduce pressure to sell immediately after harvest
questions.explanation: Storage can allow timing sales and preserve produce when conditions are suitable.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Why are dairy and poultry counted when studying agriculture and allied sectors?
options: They form important animal husbandry and farm-income activities
They are always classified as large-scale mining
questions.explanation: Animal husbandry includes production and associated farm livelihoods.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: GDP at market prices is related to GVA at basic prices by which adjustment?
options: Add product taxes and subtract product subsidies
Subtract all product taxes and add all subsidies
questions.explanation: Net taxes on products bridge these valuation concepts.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: What would measure a state's debt burden relative to its economy?
options: Share of services in total employment
Outstanding liabilities divided by GSDP for compatible periods
Expenditure divided by number of ministries
questions.explanation: A liabilities-to-GSDP ratio scales a debt stock to the size of the economy.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: Which body determines India's policy rate under the monetary policy framework?
questions.explanation: The MPC determines the policy rate required under the inflation-targeting framework.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: What is consumption of fixed capital?
options: The full value of all inventory sold
The total asset stock of households
An allowance for economic depreciation of produced fixed assets
questions.explanation: It measures the decline in asset value attributable to use and normal ageing.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which figure would show a service industry's export performance most directly?
options: Only the number of local shop licences
Physical crop output in its district
Value of its services sold to non-residents
questions.explanation: Services exports record relevant sales to non-residents.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: How do central tax devolution and specific-purpose grants differ?
options: They represent distinct transfer mechanisms with different rules
Every grant is automatically included in own tax revenue
Specific grants are always identical across states
Tax devolution is an external commercial loan
questions.explanation: Transfer categories differ by their basis and conditions.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which Andhra Pradesh budget volume is a direct starting point for planned allocations to the industries department?
options: Only an unrelated state's Outcome Budget
The detailed Industries and Commerce demand volume
A monthly RBI policy rate statement
The National Accounts Statistics methodology volume
questions.explanation: AP Finance lists the Industries and Commerce demand within its 2026–27 budget volumes.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: What boundary matters most in a State Domestic Product estimate?
options: Location of any purchaser in the world
Only the birthplace of each producer
Location of the Union finance ministry
Production within the state economy under the accounting definition
questions.explanation: State domestic product measures production attributed to a state's economy.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What does procurement refer to?
options: Every private sale at a market yard
questions.explanation: Procurement is a transaction, distinct from the MSP announcement.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What does an industrial incentive eligibility document tell applicants?
options: Which firms, activities and expenditures qualify and how to claim
The audited GSDP of every district
questions.explanation: Eligibility and claim rules should be read separately from project announcements.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: What is one purpose of regulated agricultural markets?
options: Provide an organised framework for sale and market practices
questions.explanation: Market institutions organise trading and may set market procedures.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: Which distinction is needed when comparing a Union grant and an externally aided project?
options: Both are necessarily state own-tax revenue
Different financing sources and accounting arrangements
Neither can appear in a state budget
Both are automatically the same kind of loan
questions.explanation: Track the grant or financing channel and the budget treatment.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: Which example is an own-tax receipt for a state under the GST framework?
options: A grant from the Union government
State GST on applicable intra-state supplies
questions.explanation: State GST is a state tax receipt; grants, interest and loans are different receipts.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: Using the same definitions, what happens to primary deficit if fiscal deficit stays fixed and interest payments rise?
options: It rises by the same amount
It becomes equal to total public debt
questions.explanation: Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit less interest.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: Where do foreign direct investment flows ordinarily appear in balance of payments accounting?
questions.explanation: FDI is recorded under direct investment in the financial account.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which choice best classifies software support delivered remotely?
options: An IT-enabled or software service depending on the activity
questions.explanation: Remote software-related support is broadly a service activity.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: Why is a sector's contribution to GSDP different from the budget allocation to that sector?
options: Value added measures production while allocation is public spending provision
Budget allocation determines private production one-to-one
questions.explanation: Fiscal allocation and economic value added measure different phenomena.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Which sectoral comparison helps detect whether output growth was job-intensive?
options: Only changes in nominal exchange rates
Change in employment alongside change in output
questions.explanation: Output and employment changes together illustrate the employment intensity of growth.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: What is an example of fiscal decentralisation?
options: Centralising all local service decisions in one ministry
Granting local bodies both funding and authority for assigned functions
questions.explanation: Fiscal decentralisation concerns spending and resource authority at subnational levels.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: Which measure strengthens cybersecurity without changing a department's legal mission?
options: Multi-factor authentication and documented incident response
Disabling logging for every public service
questions.explanation: Strong authentication and response procedures support resilience.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: A plant rated at 50 MW produces 600 MWh in 24 hours. What is its capacity factor?
questions.explanation: Its maximum at continuous rated power is 1,200 MWh and actual output is half of it.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which operation is suitable for many properly segregated biodegradable organics?
options: Permanent disposal in a storm drain
questions.explanation: Composting uses biological breakdown of organic materials under managed conditions.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: What do nationally determined contributions address under the Paris Agreement?
options: A requirement that every country has identical legislation
Only the management of wildlife trade
questions.explanation: NDCs are national contributions communicated in the Paris Agreement process.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which agreement focuses broadly on conservation, sustainable use and benefit sharing?
questions.explanation: Those are the core objectives of the CBD.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which is an in-situ conservation measure?
options: Maintaining specimens only in a laboratory
Protecting a species in its natural habitat
Studying preserved specimens only in a museum
Storing seeds only in an off-site bank
questions.explanation: In-situ protection maintains organisms and ecological relationships in natural settings.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: What is an example of demand-side management?
options: Shifting flexible electricity use away from peak hours
Increasing the number of generation reports only
Adding the same load at every existing peak
questions.explanation: Demand-side measures change electricity consumption or its timing.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: What historical subject does IGMDP refer to?
questions.explanation: IGMDP is the historical programme name used in India's defence technology context.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: What physical process supplies heat in conventional nuclear power reactors?
options: Combustion of coal in every reactor
questions.explanation: Fission releases heat that can be used to produce electricity.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which option is highest in a typical waste management hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Prevention avoids generating the waste in the first place.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: Which evidence best tests a biofuel's sustainability?
options: Life-cycle emissions, land and water effects and feedstock sourcing
Only the colour of the blended fuel
questions.explanation: Sustainability depends on upstream and downstream impacts.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: What is a relevant Digital India inclusion concern?
options: The number of ships in a historical fleet
Only the brand of the oldest computer
Access, connectivity and ability to use a service
questions.explanation: Access and skills affect who benefits from digital public infrastructure.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which instrument commonly sets obligations for different waste streams in India?
questions.explanation: Different waste categories are regulated through applicable laws, rules and permissions.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: What distinction matters when comparing a CITES appendix and a Red List category?
options: Trade-control status and assessed extinction risk use different frameworks
questions.explanation: CITES regulates trade, while Red List assessment concerns extinction risk.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: What makes a region qualify for hotspot designation under the commonly used approach?
options: Any landscape with low annual temperatures
Any region containing one protected building
High endemic plant diversity and substantial historical habitat loss
questions.explanation: Hotspot criteria combine endemism and substantial loss of original habitat.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: What is the main electricity-system service provided by storage in a low-demand and high-output interval?
options: Shift energy to a later interval when it is needed
questions.explanation: Storage can shift when electricity generated earlier is delivered.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: A generator delivers 25 MW for 4 hours. How much energy is delivered?
questions.explanation: Energy over the interval equals average power times elapsed time.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: How should a candidate verify the date of a new national technology policy?
options: Use the date of the first speculative report alone
Assume every draft took effect immediately
Infer it from an earlier mission's acronym
Check the official issued policy or release and its effective date
questions.explanation: Issuance and effective dates should be distinguished from discussion and draft release.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: Which Indian authority publishes installed generating capacity reports referenced in the syllabus notes?
questions.explanation: CEA publishes official power-sector capacity statistics.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: What is one common aim of a transport biofuel blending policy?
options: Substitute part of fossil fuel use with specified biofuel
Merge all fuel taxes into a property tax
questions.explanation: Blending mixes an approved biofuel with conventional fuel under specified conditions.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: Which measure counts newly occurring cases during a defined period, under specified population at risk?
questions.explanation: Incidence measures new occurrences in the population or person-time at risk.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: Why use a dated Ministry release when revising a public health programme?
options: All government programmes have identical eligibility
Features and coverage may change over time
Publication date defines disease incidence by itself
A date proves every programme objective was achieved
questions.explanation: Current programme details should be tied to the applicable release and period.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: What is Aditya-L1 primarily designed to study?
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 is India's observatory mission for studying the Sun.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which agreement regulates international trade in listed wildlife specimens?
questions.explanation: CITES regulates international trade in specimens of listed wild fauna and flora.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: Which agreement focuses specifically on the phase-out of ozone-depleting substances?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol established controls on ozone-depleting substances.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: What does a disability-adjusted life year combine?
options: Average patient travel time and inflation only
Years of life lost and years lived with disability
All diagnoses without considering duration or severity
questions.explanation: DALYs combine mortality and disability burdens in a common measure.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: Which is a non-renewable fossil energy source?
questions.explanation: Coal forms over geological time and is depleted when extracted.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which is a reason to measure pollution after a control intervention?
options: Assume all changes were successful without data
Replace all applicable source testing automatically
Determine whether environmental conditions or emissions improved
Remove the need for a prior baseline
questions.explanation: Follow-up data enables comparison with objectives and baselines.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: What causes ocean acidification principally?
options: Uptake of atmospheric carbon dioxide changes seawater carbonate chemistry
An increase in ocean salinity always creates acid rain
questions.explanation: Dissolved carbon dioxide shifts carbonate chemistry and lowers average pH.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: What is the purpose of treating wastewater before a permitted discharge?
options: Reduce pollutants and meet relevant standards
Change the identity of the receiving river
questions.explanation: Treatment can lower harmful loads under the applicable standards.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which process returns nutrients from dead organic material to an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down organic material and recycle nutrients.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which type of diversity describes genetic variation within a single crop species?
questions.explanation: Genetic diversity concerns variation within and among breeding populations.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: What happens in anaerobic digestion?
options: Airborne noise is damped in a barrier
Metals are melted into new alloys by sunlight
Organic material breaks down without free oxygen, producing biogas and digestate
Waste polymer is mechanically shredded without biological activity
questions.explanation: Anaerobic digestion is a biological process under oxygen-limited conditions.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: What can a wildlife corridor help maintain?
options: Connectivity and movement between habitat patches
A uniform temperature in every protected area
The same species count in all regions
questions.explanation: Connectivity can support movement and gene flow.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: What does endemic mean in biogeography?
options: Naturally restricted to a specified geographic area
questions.explanation: Geographic restriction defines endemism independently of threat category.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: What do Bharat Stage standards concern?
questions.explanation: Bharat Stage standards set limits on specified vehicle pollutants.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which method specifically uses biological activity to manage contaminants?
questions.explanation: Bioremediation relies on suitable organisms or biological processes to transform, remove or immobilise pollutants.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which is one threat caused by fragmentation?
options: Reduced movement between separated habitat patches
Automatic expansion of every species' range
Increased freedom of movement for every species
questions.explanation: Fragmentation can isolate populations and disrupt movement.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which example best illustrates source reduction for packaging waste?
options: Transfer the waste to another town without changing material use
Redesign packaging to use less material
Collect the same waste for final disposal only
questions.explanation: Source reduction prevents material from entering the waste stream.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which measure targets industrial air pollution at emission source?
options: Switching the units of ambient data
Appropriate emission controls and cleaner production
questions.explanation: Cleaner production and controls before release reduce emissions.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: How do the SDGs frame development?
options: They combine social, environmental and economic goals
They prescribe one local administrative map
questions.explanation: The goals span multiple dimensions of sustainable development.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: What task does public health surveillance serve?
options: Systematic monitoring and communication of health events for action
questions.explanation: Surveillance collects and interprets data to support public health action.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: What does a capacity factor express for an electricity generator?
options: Total plant area divided by regional population
Output over a period relative to continuous operation at rated output
Unit price divided by total fuel cost
Average tariff as a fraction of demand
questions.explanation: Capacity factor compares actual energy and hypothetical continuous rated generation.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: Where is the ozone layer primarily found?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer is concentrated in the stratosphere.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: What is the purpose of zoning in a biosphere reserve?
options: Exclude any local resident from every zone automatically
Manage conservation and human uses under different zone objectives
Apply the same rules to every activity everywhere
questions.explanation: Different zones organise levels and kinds of conservation and use.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: Which is a civil application of radioisotopes?
options: Obtaining internet access without a signal
questions.explanation: Suitable radioisotopes can act as tracers in diagnostic imaging.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: What type of pollution is directly related to sustained high sound levels?
questions.explanation: Sound exposures can be assessed using appropriate noise measures.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: Which measure captures existing disease cases at a specified time relative to the population?
options: Only the number of new diagnoses next year
questions.explanation: Point prevalence includes cases present at the chosen time.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: Which outcome is most directly associated with e-governance?
options: Delivery or administration of public services through digital systems
Replacement of all legal rights with software terms
questions.explanation: E-governance involves use of information systems for public administration and access.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: What is one relevant environmental assessment issue for an introduced crop trait?
options: Area of unrelated polar ice alone
The font on the first product label alone
The number of business letters archived
Exposure and possible gene flow in the receiving environment
questions.explanation: Environmental risk assessment considers the particular trait and exposure context.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: Why does a variable generation mix require system flexibility?
options: All generators always produce the same output
The physical grid no longer requires balancing
Output and demand do not necessarily align in time
questions.explanation: Flexibility helps balance supply and demand as available generation varies.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which practice helps reduce erosion on vulnerable farmland?
options: Keeping all slopes bare during heavy rainfall
questions.explanation: Cover can reduce raindrop impact and slow runoff.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Why check ambient measurements and emission data together?
options: Only one can ever use standard units
Ambient measurements guarantee one unique source
Both always report exactly the same numerical value
They answer different questions about exposure and source releases
questions.explanation: Exposure depends on emissions, other sources and dispersion or transport.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: What quality lets two public-service systems exchange and use compatible data?
questions.explanation: Interoperability makes systems work together through compatible data and interfaces.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: Which action is primarily climate mitigation?
options: Preparing heat shelters for existing exposure
Reducing fossil electricity emissions by switching to a lower-emission source
Changing a crop calendar to manage drought
questions.explanation: Mitigation addresses emissions or removals, rather than adjustment to impacts.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which is an ex-situ conservation measure?
options: Restoration of the original wetland only
A seed bank storing viable material away from its origin
In-place protection of an entire river catchment
Regulating visitors within an active national park only
questions.explanation: Ex-situ methods maintain material outside its native habitat.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: What is a reasonable indicator of access to primary care?
options: Whether people can obtain needed essential services within practical constraints
questions.explanation: Availability, affordability and practical ability to use services determine access.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: What does species richness count?
options: Total number of individuals of one species
Number of species within a defined assemblage
questions.explanation: Richness counts species rather than individual organisms or their abundance distribution.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: What is the function of a satellite launch vehicle?
options: Operate all of the satellite's ground data services
Determine the topics in national science policy
Deliver a payload to its planned trajectory or orbit
questions.explanation: The launch vehicle places payloads on the required flight path.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Why segregate waste at source?
options: Eliminate the need for safe handling procedures
Keep streams suitable for appropriate processing
questions.explanation: Segregation reduces cross-contamination and supports treatment or recovery.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: Which is a renewable primary energy source?
questions.explanation: Wind is replenished by atmospheric processes.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: What is the principal demonstrated capability of Chandrayaan-3?
options: Observing a solar eclipse from Earth orbit only
Soft landing and roving on the Moon
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 demonstrated safe lunar landing and roving.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: What measure describes the highest instantaneous load in a time period?
questions.explanation: Peak demand describes the maximum power required over the interval considered.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which organism is a primary producer in a typical pond food chain?
options: A fish that eats other organisms
An insect larva feeding on detritus
questions.explanation: Producers make organic material from inorganic sources using an energy source such as light.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: Which application most directly uses earth-observation imagery?
options: Monitoring land cover or crop conditions
Calculating the terms of a loan contract
questions.explanation: Images can be analysed for spatial and temporal features of land and vegetation.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: Which is an abiotic component of a freshwater ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Abiotic components are nonliving environmental factors.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: Which mission is associated with Mars exploration by ISRO?
questions.explanation: ISRO's Mars Orbiter Mission carried out an interplanetary mission to Mars.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: What is a direct preparedness measure for a health emergency?
options: Waiting to organise care until after peak demand
Using a budget figure as a substitute for operational plans
questions.explanation: Preparedness identifies resources and coordination before demand surges.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: What does DRDO primarily do at an institutional level?
questions.explanation: DRDO is India's defence research and development organisation.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: Which site factor can affect feasibility of bioremediation?
options: Whether conditions support useful biological activity for the contaminant
Only the name of the road nearby
The number of unrelated tax filings
Whether the site has an election booth
questions.explanation: Biological treatment depends on compatibility among organisms, conditions and pollutants.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: Why can renewable capacity share differ from renewable generation share?
options: Renewables are measured only in tonnes
Every plant follows the exact same operating schedule
Generators operate at different capacity factors
Capacity and generation are always equal
questions.explanation: Capacity measures rated power while generation reflects actual energy over time.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: What does an installed capacity of 100 MW describe?
questions.explanation: MW is a rate of energy production, while generation over time is measured in MWh.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: Which is an example of climate adaptation?
options: Replacing fossil power solely to cut emissions
Redesigning drainage for stronger rainfall events
questions.explanation: Adaptation reduces harm from current or expected impacts.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: Which organisation leads India's civilian space programmes?
questions.explanation: ISRO is the national space agency under the Department of Space.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: Which pollutants are major precursors of acid deposition?
questions.explanation: These oxides can form acidic products in the atmosphere.

title: Mains Paper II · Syllabus sampler
provenance: GateLabs original questions. One question per Annexure II syllabus unit across both sections.

questions.topic: National Income, Planning and Economic Reform
questions.question: Gross domestic product is ₹6,400 crore, consumption of fixed capital is ₹760 crore and net primary income from abroad is +₹120 crore. What is net national income at the same valuation on this simplified basis?
questions.explanation: Convert domestic to national by adding ₹120 crore. Convert gross to net by deducting ₹760 crore. The result is 6,400 + 120 − 760 = ₹5,760 crore.

questions.topic: Money, Banking, Public Finance and External Accounts
questions.question: A foreign investor buys newly issued equity in a resident firm. In a subsequent period the firm pays that investor dividends. How are the two cross-border flows classified?
options: Equity acquisition in the financial account and dividends in current-account primary income
Equity acquisition in primary income and dividends in the financial account
Equity acquisition in services and dividends in secondary income
questions.explanation: The equity acquisition changes a financial asset or liability. The dividend is investment income, which belongs to the current account.

questions.topic: Indian Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: Crop A’s cultivated area falls from 1,000 to 800 hectares, while output rises from 2,000 to 2,160 tonnes. By what percentage does average yield rise?
questions.explanation: Yield rises from 2 to 2.7 tonnes per hectare. Use the original yield as the base: (2.7 − 2)/2 = 35%.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh GSDP and State Finances
questions.question: A state scheme’s budget estimate is ₹250 crore, revised estimate ₹220 crore and audited expenditure ₹198 crore. Which comparison measures the shortfall against the original allocation, and by how much?
options: Revised estimate versus audited actual; ₹22 crore
Budget estimate versus audited actual; ₹52 crore
Budget estimate versus revised estimate; ₹30 crore
Audited actual versus budget estimate; ₹48 crore
questions.explanation: The question asks about actual spending compared with the original budget. The relevant difference is 250 − 198 = ₹52 crore.

questions.topic: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture, Industry and Services
questions.question: A producer cooperative already has a cold room. Produce warms up for six hours in transport before reaching it, and most new spoilage occurs during this interval. Which intervention targets the identified bottleneck most directly?
options: Increasing cold-room capacity while keeping the same warm journey
Refrigerated transport or precooling that maintains suitable temperatures through the journey
Publishing wholesale price alerts with the same handling schedule
Adding faster packing equipment after the produce reaches the cold room
questions.explanation: The identified losses arise before storage. Interventions that protect produce during the warm transit stage target the cause.

questions.topic: Indian Science, Technology and Public Missions
questions.question: Two missions are proposed: one to monitor changes in the solar corona and one to survey crop conditions in Andhra Pradesh. Which pairing of observational objectives is sound?
options: Repeated thermal surveys of cultivated land for the corona, and solar emission records for crops
A single broad solar measurement is sufficient for both objectives
Both objectives are met by mapping only Earth’s magnetic field at the surface
Continuous solar monitoring for the corona, and repeated spatial observations of Earth’s surface for crops
questions.explanation: The first objective targets solar atmospheric activity. The second requires spatial observations of terrestrial vegetation at multiple times.

questions.topic: Energy Management, Renewables and Bharat Stage Rules
questions.question: A 100 MW renewable plant produces 1,200 MWh over a 24-hour day. What is its capacity factor over this interval?
questions.explanation: The maximum at rated output is 100 × 24 = 2,400 MWh. Actual energy divided by the interval maximum is 1,200/2,400 = 50%.

questions.topic: Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Conservation
questions.question: A wildlife specimen is sought for international commercial sale. The species appears in an appendix of a wildlife-trade treaty. Which statement best captures the first regulatory question?
options: Treat all international sales as automatically allowed if the source country issues a domestic receipt.
Assume the listing sets a uniform market price for the specimen.
Check the relevant listing and the shipment’s purpose to determine applicable permits or restrictions.
Apply the same conditions as for an unlisted species because the shipment is commercial.
questions.explanation: CITES trade controls depend on the listed species, its appendix and the nature of the proposed movement.

questions.topic: Waste, Pollution and Environmental Remediation
questions.question: A contaminated site has biodegradable organic pollutants. Pilot plots receiving oxygen and nutrients show faster decreases than equally sampled untreated plots. Which mechanism is the intervention primarily testing?
options: Physical removal of contaminants by excavation
Separation of pollutants by sieving the soil
Isolation of contaminants beneath an impermeable barrier
Stimulation of microbes that break down the pollutant
questions.explanation: The supplied oxygen and nutrients can support microbial metabolism of the biodegradable contaminant. Excavation, sieving and capping rely on other mechanisms.

questions.topic: Climate, Sustainable Development and Public Health
questions.question: A refrigerant change nearly eliminates ozone depletion potential but the replacement has a high global warming potential. Which conclusion follows?
options: It addresses ozone depletion, while its climate impact needs a separate assessment.
Low ozone depletion potential guarantees negligible warming.
Ozone depletion potential measures carbon emissions during manufacture.
A high global warming potential proves the replacement has high ozone depletion potential.
questions.explanation: ODP estimates effect on stratospheric ozone. GWP describes climate forcing over a chosen time horizon. A lower value of one does not determine the other.
